drug_indication: Advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer
catalyst_text: Received RMAT designation from FDA for NSCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA granted RMAT designation to KB707 for advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. This designation is intended to expedite development and offers benefits such as rolling review and intensive FDA guidance, potentially shortening time to approval. Early clinical evidence from the ongoing KYANITE-1 study of inhaled therapy supported the designation.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Krystal Biotech, Inc. (the “Company”) (NASDAQ:KRYS) announced today that the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation to KB707, the Company’s redosable immunotherapy designed to drive sustained, localized expression of interleukin-2 and interleukin-12 in the tumor microenvironment, for the treatment of advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).” “The designation provides all the benefits of the FDA’s Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations, including potential for rolling review, intensive FDA guidance and interaction, and organizational commitment from senior managers at the FDA, as well as the ability to work more closely and frequently with the FDA to discuss innovative trial designs, surrogate or intermediate endpoints to support potential accelerated approval, and novel approaches to satisfy post-approval requirements.” “Data to support the FDA’s RMAT designation included early clinical evidence from the Company’s ongoing KYANITE-1 study that demonstrated consistent and meaningful antitumor activity, including durable responses and clinically significant tumor reductions, in patients with heavily pre-treated advanced NSCLC receiving inhaled KB707.”

catalyst_text: Announced positive interim results and submitted study design
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive interim molecular and safety data from the highest-dose cohort of the Phase 1 CORAL-1 trial in cystic fibrosis, confirming lung delivery and expression of wild-type CFTR with broad airway transduction. Transduction ranged from 29.4% to 42.1% across patients and treatment was generally well tolerated, with one bronchoscopy-related SAE. The registrational repeat-dosing CORAL-3 study design was submitted to the FDA in late December to support advancement.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Krystal Biotech, Inc. … today announced a positive interim clinical update from the highest dose cohort of CORAL-1 … confirming the successful lung delivery and expression of wild-type cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein following inhaled administration of KB407.” “As of the 2026-01-06 data cut-off, a total of seven (7) patients have been dosed with KB407 in the highest dose Cohort 3 of CORAL-1… KB407 transduction was confirmed in all Cohort 3 patients with successful bronchoscopies… ranging from 29.4% to 42.1% across these six patients.” “Consistent with the safety profile previously reported from Cohorts 1 and 2, inhaled KB407 continued to be well tolerated by patients treated with the highest dose in Cohort 3.” “The Company submitted the CORAL-3 study design to the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in late December.”
